sections.content:
50,195 people

were counted on the census as "project support officers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Project support officers assist in the organisation, planning, monitoring and direction of a project and ensure it is adequately resourced and on schedule.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "project support officers", 17.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "project support officers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "project support officers" included:

  • IT user support technicians
  • customer service supervisors
  • finance and investment analysts and advisers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "project support officers" there were more women than men (63.3% compared with 36.7%).

This means "project support officers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 36.7% and women made up 63.3% of "project support officers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "project support officers" included:

  • charitable organisation managers and directors
  • pharmacists
  • call and contact centre occupations

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "project support officers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "project support officers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "project support officers", 10.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (82.6% compared with 17.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96.2%) than self-employed (3.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
